Note: the worker is already in zombie state. We just missed the notification.
```
(gdb) p worker->state
$3 = 3
```

(in response to https://github.com/google/iree/pull/8872#issuecomment-1098230288)
huh that's odd - notification await should work like that (it should call the condition function before waiting and then if anything posts a change between when it has checked and when it waits it'll loop again). The futex emulation (what's used with tsan) may have a bug in it - it may be worth revisiting that (I think today it's half of the futex code and then some pthread alternate paths spliced in, but it's probably worth having a separate copy that follows pthread conventions more).

The `await` looks fine it itself, but in the surrounding code in `iree_task_worker_deinitialize`, something is missing to prevent the thread from exiting before we reach the `await`. See https://github.com/google/iree/pull/8872#issuecomment-1098230288

that should be fine - the zombie flag will be set:
https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/iree/task/worker.c#L376-L378

and then the await will immediately return as its condition (is_zombie) will be satisfied:
https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/iree/task/worker.c#L110-L115

(in other words - it's expected that calling in to await on a condition that is true is fine - so there's no harm if the worker exits before we await - unless the implementation of await for pthreads has a bug)

I still don't see anything preventing this ordering of events:

1. The main thread reads the worker state  ([link](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/519815e4bcd51cf690ede07338d73d99241465b7/iree/base/internal/synchronization.c#L683), evaluating the `condition_fn` here that is `iree_task_worker_is_zombie`). That returns false, so the main thread will enter the wait.
2. The worker thread changes to zombie state [link](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/519815e4bcd51cf690ede07338d73d99241465b7/iree/task/worker.c#L376).
3. The worker thread posts the notification [link](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/519815e4bcd51cf690ede07338d73d99241465b7/iree/task/worker.c#L378)
4. The main thread enters the wait [link](https://github.com/google/iree/blob/519815e4bcd51cf690ede07338d73d99241465b7/iree/base/internal/synchronization.c#L688), as previously decided at step 1. It already missed the notification from step 3.
yes, that's what I'm saying: that is _not_ the behavior of the futex implementation, but may be the behavior of the pthread implementation. It should be fixed.

Sorry, I'm confused. In the previous comments, steps 2 and 3 link to `iree_notification_await`. I thought that was still in the code that's shared between futex / pthread implementations - the divergence seems to happen in `iree_notification_commit_wait`, which it does call.

Your confusion is confusing me :)
By contract it is safe to call iree_notification_await when the condition is already satisfied.
The futex implementation properly handles this.
The pthread implementation doesn't seem to (looking at https://github.com/google/iree/blob/main/iree/base/internal/synchronization.c#L633-L636).
The pthread implementation needs to be fixed.

My concern (https://github.com/google/iree/issues/8871#issuecomment-1098276882) is what if the condition is **concurrently** made satisfied while `iree_notification_await` is running - so that the atomic store of worker state and the notification post (steps 2 and 3 above) both occur after `iree_notification_await` performed the atomic read of worker state (step 1) and before it committed the wait (step 4)?
oooh i get it now! I'll fix the pthreads path. thanks for the explanation!
I can take a whack at it too unless you'd like to get your hands dirty with it - I'm super appreciative of you finding these issues and don't mean to force the fixes onto you too :)
I was taking a look --- how does this look? https://github.com/google/iree/pull/8876
If that fixes the issue then that's awesome! I may rejigger the code to make it easier to follow (less mixing of atomics and mutex stuff) and that'd be a more confident NFC if you do this first :)

it is looking ok in a ctest run with 1000 repeats and it certainly matches my understanding, now that i understand the above explanation, that it fixes a specific issue in the existing code (as explained in the comment added by that pr).
wait, no indeed it was written hastily and incorrect. i am missing a really good way to test this code ---- i'll have to compensate with lots of care.

Does this help make things easier to read? It has your fix for locking but may not work for the same reason you found:
https://github.com/google/iree/commit/d9521a7715adf37cca20989fb017aabc3765f4cd
(untested, just code golfing while waiting for lunch delivery :)

After all my #8876 was correct, my above comment https://github.com/google/iree/issues/8871#issuecomment-1098380562 was incorrect in calling it incorrect, and your https://github.com/google/iree/commit/d9521a7715adf37cca20989fb017aabc3765f4cd is correct too for the same reason, and yes it is clearer - i was also thinking while reading this code that it would help to decouple the different implementations in this way.
cool - sent https://github.com/google/iree/pull/8877 - will see what the bots say!
I believe we've quashed this now. Or, at least this specific one :P

issue.body:
This reproduces every ~1000 runs of `dylib` unit tests:
```
ctest -j20 -R iree/hal/dylib/cts/dylib --repeat-until-fail 1000 --output-on-failure
```

The test just hangs. Attaching GDB to it, I get [this stack](https://gist.github.com/bjacob/04bf9cd81f4ddf7786f4c0af0de3141c). According to GDB there is no other thread anymore (other than a TSan-internal thread) --- this is a single-threaded program at this point.

So `iree_task_worker_deinitialize` is awating a notification,

```
  if (worker->thread) {
    iree_notification_await(&worker->state_notification,
                            (iree_condition_fn_t)iree_task_worker_is_zombie,
                            worker, iree_infinite_timeout());
  }
```

but it will never come as there is no other thread left to send it.

issue.title: Shutdown deadlock in `iree_task_worker_deinitialize` -> `iree_notification_await` as the thread is already gone

```
(gdb) p worker->state
$3 = 3
```

issue.body:
This seems to be fixing #8863.

This prevents new steals from starting while we wait for workers to reach zombie state.

What I don't understand at the moment is whether this always prevents ongoing steals from continuing past the point where the victim reaches zombie state. That's what I want to prevent, and this seems to be prevented in 1000 runs of tests with TSan, but I don't understand if that's guaranteed to be prevented.

I can make up half rationales of the form "a worker only reaches zombie state if it had nothing to work on anymore, so it has nothing to steal from at that point" but the fine details of how that's synchronized with `try_steal` are not clear to me. I understand that `try_steal` won't start a steal if the load-acquire of `worker_live_mask` returns 0 for this worker's bit, but I don't understand what happens if `try_steal` was already past that point by the time we clear that bit.

Fixes #8863.
